transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I suppose it’s probably a bit silly, but… I’ve realized I’m arranging things at home around not having to see spiders. Like, I’ll put off doing laundry because it means going down to the basement, and I avoid the garden shed. I’ve even paid people to do small jobs that I really do know how to do myself, just because I can’t quite make myself go into those spaces. It’s embarrassing, but it’s starting to feel like I’m working around it all the time.
When you see a spider, do you feel an immediate surge of intense fear?

Yes… I mean, I wish I could say I just dislike them, but if I actually see one, it’s immediate. My chest tightens, my hands start shaking, and I sort of freeze in the doorway—or I back away very quickly before I’ve even really thought about it. It feels a bit ridiculous saying that, but that’s what happens.
Is your fear limited to spiders, or do you find yourself feeling this same kind of intense fear around lots of other things too?

Mostly spiders, really. I don’t think I’m like this about lots of things. I mean, I know a spider in the corner of an old house probably isn’t going to hurt me, and I can say that sensibly sitting here… but the moment I imagine one dropping out of a box or sitting near the washer, it just feels huge and threatening. Which sounds dramatic, I know, but that’s the thing that sets me off.
